answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a trust graph in which every identity is a vertex linked to past work and a refundable stake. A new vertex gains no trading power until peers confirm completed tasks and the stake stays locked through a cooling period. Creating thousands of fake vertices needs large capital or months of work, while fraud forfeits the stake. This turns a nebula of accounts into a checkable network: each identity must earn its edges, and suspicious clusters are visible before they can move markets. No ivory-tower shortcut grants trust; only proven behaviour does.
